result:
I found 12 rules where the code didn't match the docstring, fixed all of them in `pricebook.py`, and now all 150 rules match. To check, I built a reference calculation from each docstring and compared it with every rule over many quantities and unit prices. That check found exactly these 12, the same ones I spotted by reading the code. After the fixes it finds none.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 04 | The 50,000-won cap only applied once the discount went over 100,000 | Cap always applies |
| 07 | The 30,000-won cap only applied once the discount went over 60,000 | Cap always applies |
| 58 | The 10,000-won cap only applied once the discount went over 20,000 | Cap always applies |
| 15 | Discount started at 21 units | Starts at 20 |
| 41 | Discount started at 13 units | Starts at 12 |
| 66 | Discount started above 12 units (`>`) | Starts at 12 (`>=`) |
| 16 | The cap was applied to the price, not the discount | Discount is capped at 100,000 won |
| 117 | The cap was applied to the price, not the discount | Discount is capped at 10,000 won |
| 21 | A marginal rule discounted the full amount | Discount is now `(qty-12)*unit` |
| 59 | Discount was rounded with `round()` | Floored with `//` |
| 72 | Discount was rounded with `round()` | Floored with `//` |
| 136 | Rate was 6% | 5%, as documented |

In each case I changed the code to match the docstring and left the docstrings as they were.

STATUS: DONE
